intro.title: Build request logging middleware
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a request logging middleware for a Node.js server. You will learn how to intercept incoming HTTP requests, log details like the request method and URL, and pass control to the next handler. The core concept is middleware—a function that processes requests in a pipeline. You'll use Node.js's built-in HTTP module and basic JavaScript functions. By the end, you'll have a working logger that outputs request information to the console.
intro.usecase: Request logging middleware is essential for monitoring and debugging production Node.js applications. In e-commerce platforms like Shopify or payment systems like Stripe, every API request is logged to track user activity, detect suspicious patterns, and troubleshoot errors. This pattern appears in admin dashboards where developers view request metrics, in security audit logs that record access attempts, and in error reporting panels that help teams identify and fix issues quickly. Implementing this middleware gives you visibility into how your application behaves in real-world scenarios.
